close_reason: documented in from_cert rustdoc; TryFrom is the strict path
description: Trigger: trust anchor cert has NameConstraints extension marked critical=true, but its DER value fails to parse (e.g., encoding corruption, unsupported encoding form, or future extension format). from_cert calls find_cert_ext which silently returns None on parse error, so name_constraints = None. chain_walk proceeds with no NC constraints applied. Bad behavior: a critical extension that the implementation cannot process is silently ignored instead of causing rejection. RFC 5280 §4.2 requires: 'A certificate-using system MUST reject the certificate if it encounters a critical extension it does not recognize or a critical extension that it cannot process.' OID_NAME_CONSTRAINTS is in HANDLED_CRITICAL_OIDS (so check_critical_extensions passes), but the parse error in find_cert_ext means the extension content is not actually processed — the implementation cannot enforce it, yet does not reject. Note: PKIX-onc.4 covers the documentation angle; this is the RFC 5280 correctness violation. The TryFrom<Certificate> path is fail-closed and correct; from_cert is the unsafe path.
title: from_cert fail-open silently drops critical NC: RFC 5280 §4.2 violation
